smell: Sibling constructors inconsistently pick positional args vs functional options. okd.New/executor.New/proxmox.New/terraform.New/K8sClient use variadic Option; addon.NewManager and phase.NewBasePhase take four positional args each. The four-arg positional form becomes an argument-order footgun as fields grow, and diverges from the dominant idiom across the rest of the module.
severity_reason: Consistency finding; no correctness risk but each new field at addon.NewManager or NewBasePhase breaks every caller and the callers already stitch in identical executor/logger wiring.
fix_summary: Migrate addon.NewManager and phase.NewBasePhase to the variadic Option idiom used elsewhere: `func NewManager(cfg *config.Config, opts ...ManagerOption) *Manager` with WithExecutor/WithLogger/WithProjectRoot, matching okd.New. Keeps one ManagerOption helper per field; the existing three call sites adapt trivially.
rule_source: Go proverb: 'clear is better than clever'
must_preserve: All existing fields (cfg, exec, logger, projectRoot) remain functionally required — only the call shape changes.

smell: okd.WithEnv has an order-dependency contract hidden in New: if WithEnv runs before WithLogger, WithEnv creates the executor early and New re-runs WithLogger on it after the option loop. Option functions should be commutative — callers should be free to pass them in any order without the constructor compensating.
severity_reason: The compensation works today but encodes a subtle ordering contract into New. A future option (e.g. WithWorkDir that also lazy-builds) replicates the same dance.
fix_summary: Defer executor construction until after the option loop: have WithEnv store `pendingEnv []string` on *Provisioner, then build `p.executor = executor.New(executor.WithLogger(p.logger), executor.WithEnv(p.pendingEnv))` once in New. Options stay pure setters; the constructor owns ordering.
rule_source: Uber Go Style Guide §Functional Options (options should be commutative)
must_preserve: logutil.NopLogger default behavior and the 'env appended after os.Environ' semantics of executor.WithEnv.

smell: SetupKubeconfig performs filesystem I/O (FileExists, env mutation) but omits context.Context, while every other exported method on *Phase (Execute, DeployInfrastructure, WaitForBootstrap, MonitorInstallation, SetupClusterAccess, StartWorkerVMs, ValidateClusterAccess) takes ctx first. The asymmetry blocks callers from cancelling the sequence uniformly and breaks the ctx-first discipline on the exported Phase surface.
severity_reason: Minimal current-harm (filesystem op is fast) but the signature is out of family with sibling Phase methods and blocks future I/O (e.g., writing a sentinel) from honoring cancellation.
fix_summary: Change signature to `func (p *Phase) SetupKubeconfig(ctx context.Context, clusterDir string) error`. Update the single call site in internal/distribution/okd/install/steps.go to pass ctx. Matches SetupClusterAccess in the same phase (which takes ctx even though it currently ignores it).
rule_source: Google Go Style Guide §Contexts ('context.Context should be the first argument of exported functions that do I/O or may block')
must_preserve: Canonical call site at install/steps.go StepSetupKubeconfig; must still mutate p.Exec.Env so downstream subprocesses inherit KUBECONFIG.

smell: Minimum control-plane resource constants live in two packages with the same values but diverging disk-size number. okd.MinControlPlaneDiskGB=50 matches config.MinDiskGBControlPlaneOKD=50 so the okd constants exist only so Validate can produce a different error message — config already validates resources during load. Two sources of truth for the same limit.
severity_reason: Both sets currently agree; but a future OKD-version bump will almost certainly update one and drift. config package is the canonical location (it already runs the validator during loader.LoadFile).
fix_summary: Delete okd.MinControlPlane* constants and Provisioner.Validate's resource-min checks; rely on config.ValidateOKDConfig which is already invoked via cfg.Validate() during setup. Alternatively import config.MinCPUControlPlaneOKD / MinMemoryMBControlPlaneOKD / MinDiskGBControlPlaneOKD in okd.Validate. Net: one constant set.
rule_source: Go proverb: 'a little copying is better than a little dependency' — but only when copies don't drift; here they will
CLAUDE.md §architecture-notes (BasePhase/config as single sources of truth)
must_preserve: All three numeric values (8192, 4, 50) must remain the enforced minimum — just declared once.

smell: Phase NewOptions factory shapes diverge across siblings. setup.DefaultOptions(projectRoot) takes ONLY projectRoot; install.NewOptions, postinstall.NewOptions, destroy.NewOptions take (cfg, projectRoot). install.NewOptions pulls eight fields from cfg; setup.DefaultOptions ignores cfg entirely, leaving the caller to set opts.OKDReleaseBaseURL in okd.go. Same-package verb; three different contracts.
severity_reason: Purely consistency. Callers hand-stitch the missing cfg plumbing for setup, which is exactly the job NewOptions does elsewhere.
fix_summary: Rename setup.DefaultOptions to setup.NewOptions(cfg, projectRoot) and fold ResolveReleaseBaseURL into it. Matches the (cfg, projectRoot) signature the other three phase packages share. Single call site in okd.go.
rule_source: Uber §API Design (consistent constructor naming across sibling packages)
must_preserve: The setup Options zero-value behavior and the ResolveReleaseBaseURL env-override precedence.

smell: cleanup.Execute takes *Options whose zero Kind yields a bare error 'unknown cleanup type: ' with no friendly message. Worse, an Options{} zero-value (no Logger, no Kind) will default to NopLogger and return an error with no hint that Kind was unset. Either make the zero value valid (default to Full) or reject nil/empty Kind up front with a named error.
severity_reason: Edge case — the three call sites (okd.go Prepare, destroy steps, standalone destroy) all set Kind explicitly. But the struct is exported with a zero-value footgun.
fix_summary: Add an exported `var ErrKindNotSet = errors.New(...)` sentinel and have Execute return it wrapped when opts.Kind == ''. Alternatively, switch to `NewOptions(kind Kind) *Options` so the required field is a constructor parameter, mirroring destroy.NewOptions / install.NewOptions.
rule_source: Uber §API Design 'make zero values useful or reject invalid construction'
must_preserve: All five Kind enumeration values (Full, WorkOnly, WebOnly, HAProxyOnly, TerraformOnly); Logger fallback to NopLogger.

smell: firewall.Configure and firewall.RemoveRules are exported but every in-tree caller uses the okd-specific wrappers ConfigureOKD / RemoveOKDRules. RemoveRules(HAProxyFrontendPorts(), ...) is the one exception — a single call in postinstall/haproxy.go. Configure has no direct caller. The pair is shaped like a 'future distro swap' API; flag as scaffolding but note Configure is unreferenced.
severity_reason: Scaffolding-shaped: if Configure exists, RemoveRules stays; they map to a future 'configure arbitrary port set' CLI path (symmetric API).
fix_summary: Verify intent — are Configure/RemoveRules expected entry points for a future non-OKD distro? If yes, keep and document the layering. If no, inline Configure into ConfigureOKD and keep RemoveRules (still has one external caller).
rule_source: MEMORY.md §scaffolding (symmetric API: Configure exists, RemoveRules stays)
CLAUDE.md §architecture-notes (package-level helpers live in producer pkg)
must_preserve: validatePort allowlist; both wrappers' current behavior.

smell: cleanup.GenerateSummary and cleanup.Summary struct are exported but the only caller is the package-private printSummary(). No external caller. The function is shaped like a public status-query but without a symmetric sibling (no cleanup.Verify or similar), so it does not cleanly fit scaffolding.
severity_reason: Possibly shaped for a future `okdctl cleanup status` CLI verb; defer to owner rather than deleting. No correctness impact.
fix_summary: Either unexport (GenerateSummary -> generateSummary, Summary -> summary) if no CLI surface planned, or keep both exported and add a one-line doc-comment pointing to the intended caller (e.g. 'used by okdctl cleanup status; see roadmap.md').
rule_source: Uber §Exported Surface ('do not export without a caller')
MEMORY.md §scaffolding (not symmetric — no matching verb in cleanup/)
must_preserve: The current behavior when printSummary runs at the end of Execute.

smell: OKDVersionFetcher.GetLatestForMinor is exported with no caller. GetLatestStable (paired sibling) has none either — only FetchVersions is called. Both are shaped like a symmetric-API trio (FetchVersions / GetLatestStable / GetLatestForMinor) for a future `okdctl releases list --minor 4.18` verb.
severity_reason: Scaffolding: symmetric API with a single consumed member (FetchVersions). Future CLI verb 'releases latest' is a plausible caller.
fix_summary: Verify intent against roadmap.md — if a `okdctl releases latest [--minor N.M]` command is planned, keep both. Otherwise demote to private helpers. Do not delete without checking with owner.
must_preserve: FetchVersions (has a caller) and the disk cache behavior.

smell: OKDVersion.ShortVersion is exported with no caller in the repo. DisplayName and Major/Minor are used by wizard/steps and cli/releases; ShortVersion is not. Shaped like a symmetric 'version formatting' trio but currently standalone.
severity_reason: Scaffolding: symmetric with DisplayName/Major/Minor (all are view helpers on OKDVersion).
fix_summary: Verify — if docs/releases plan a short-form version display, keep. If not, delete. No API impact either way because ShortVersion has zero external references.
must_preserve: DisplayName, Major, Minor semantics.

smell: Phase.ValidateClusterAccess, Phase.SetupClusterAccess, Phase.SetupKubeconfig are exported on *Phase in the install package. The only callers are the same package's steps.go. Since Phase is itself exported and these are phase-public methods called by a user-facing `okd.Provisioner`, they fit a future-CLI-verb shape ('okdctl cluster access', 'okdctl kubeconfig-setup'). Flagged as scaffolding.
severity_reason: Scaffolding: shaped like future-CLI-verb (e.g. `okdctl cluster access verify`). Keeping per MEMORY.md §scaffolding.
fix_summary: Verify intent — do any planned subcommands call these? If yes, keep exported and document. If no, unexport (validateClusterAccess) to reduce package surface.
must_preserve: The step.go callers' behavior; the deploy-time chown semantics in SetupClusterAccess.

smell: terraform package exports two constructors — New(workDir, opts...) and NewWithVarFile(workDir, varFile, opts...) — that differ only in one default. The second is a thin wrapper solely to preset VarFile. Idiomatic Go replaces this with a WithVarFile Option (already present-style in WithLogger/WithEnv/WithVerbose), keeping one constructor.
severity_reason: Clean constructor surface without functional change. Two constructors for the same type is the classic 'option drift' smell.
fix_summary: Add `func WithVarFile(path string) Option` that sets e.VarFile. Delete NewWithVarFile. Migrate the two call sites to terraform.New(dir, terraform.WithVarFile(varFile), ...opts).
must_preserve: Default VarFile = workDir/terraform.tfvars when WithVarFile is not provided.

smell: Provider struct has public methods (Connect, Disconnect, Provision, setupTerraform) but the project has no interface abstraction at any consumer site — cli/helpers.go and install/phase.go take the concrete *okd.Provisioner. If a non-Proxmox provider is ever on the roadmap, the Go idiom is to define the interface in the CONSUMER package (e.g. `distribution.InfrastructureProvider`), not the producer. Not a bug — a stance check per the scaffolding rule.
severity_reason: Not a defect today — Proxmox is the only supported infrastructure. Flag as guidance for the next provider (roadmap mentions other options).
fix_summary: If/when a second provider lands, define `type InfrastructureProvider interface { Connect(ctx, *Config) error; Provision(ctx, *Config, ProvisionOptions) (*ProvisionResult, error); Disconnect(ctx) error }` in the distribution package (the consumer). Proxmox implements it structurally — no code change in proxmox/. Do NOT preemptively add the interface now — Go proverb: 'accept interfaces, return structs' applies at the consumer.
must_preserve: No change today; this is a forward-looking note for when a second provider is introduced.

smell: internal/distribution is the declared 'step orchestration facade' per CLAUDE.md, but internal/cli/helpers.go imports internal/distribution/okd/okd concretely — the okd package is the only real implementation. The facade in internal/distribution/ never abstracts the distribution choice (no registry, no factory). If this is intentional (single-distro tool), okd.go's role as 'the only distribution' should be reflected in a doc comment there rather than leaving the facade incomplete.
severity_reason: The package hierarchy suggests multi-distro support but only one exists. Either the facade should register the distro (distribution.Provisioners[cfg.Distribution.Type]) or its absence should be documented.
fix_summary: Option A (minimal): add a doc-comment to internal/distribution/okd/okd.go's `Package okd` block stating 'the only distribution currently supported; internal/distribution is the orchestration package, not a provider facade'. Option B (expand scope): introduce distribution.Provisioner interface and a Register call from okd/init.
rule_source: Go proverb: 'clear is better than clever' (state the shape explicitly)
must_preserve: CLAUDE.md §architecture-notes — canonical StepDef/BuildSteps remain in internal/distribution.

smell: cluster.NewK8sClient reads KUBECONFIG from os.Getenv at construction time, then builds the cmd runner. This couples the constructor to process env state at call time and means an Exec.Env mutation elsewhere (install.Phase.SetupKubeconfig appends KUBECONFIG= to Exec.Env) is NOT seen by a later-constructed K8sClient. The doc comment on SetupKubeconfig already warns about this. The pattern should be either documented as intentional or converted to lazy evaluation.
severity_reason: Documented footgun surfaces each time a new K8sClient is constructed post-SetupKubeconfig. Low chance of regression because call pattern is fixed today.
fix_summary: Move the os.Getenv('KUBECONFIG') read inside c.run — evaluate the env lazily on each exec.Run so a mid-process KUBECONFIG mutation IS seen. Alternatively drop the env fallback and require WithKubeconfig explicitly (one call site would need the explicit pass). Either way, delete the 'warning comment' at install/phase.go:L134-L137.
rule_source: Uber Go §API Design (no surprising late-binding on constructors)
must_preserve: The 'oc' over 'kubectl' fallback and the WithCLI/WithKubeconfig/WithLogger options.

smell: phase.ExternalToolBinaries has one in-tree caller (cleanup/packages.go InstalledBinaries). Exported for the sole purpose of avoiding a setup→cleanup import. The function sits awkwardly in phase/paths.go when it exposes a property of setup (what setup installed), not of the phase base type. Consider moving to a dedicated phase/tools.go or documenting the intent inline.
severity_reason: Low cost; the name is fine and the single-caller path explains why it is exported. Might still benefit from a dedicated file so setup.go doesn't have to grep phase/paths.go.
fix_summary: Move ExternalToolBinaries to a new phase/tools.go with a one-line doc clarifying 'these binaries are installed by setup; cleanup removes them.' No callsite change.
rule_source: CLAUDE.md §architecture-notes (shared cross-phase helpers live in phase/)
Go proverb: 'clear is better than clever'
must_preserve: The list of binaries (yq, helm, sops) and the cleanup caller.

smell: Step / Skipper / FatalChecker / StepCallbacks are four interfaces that ProvisioningStep always composes together. The builtStep impl implements all four. The Orchestrator never accepts a bare Step or bare Skipper — it only accepts ProvisioningStep. Four interfaces where one (or two) would serve; none are consumed at the bare type by non-test code.
severity_reason: Not a correctness issue. The split is load-bearing ONLY if the orchestrator (or a future consumer) will accept a bare Step. Today it does not.
fix_summary: Keep Step (the 'id+name+execute' core could plausibly stand alone). Inline Skipper, FatalChecker, StepCallbacks into ProvisioningStep directly. Net: three interface decls removed, callers unaffected. Alternatively, leave as-is if a future test helper wants to accept just Skipper — document that intent on each interface.
rule_source: Go proverb: 'the bigger the interface, the weaker the abstraction' (applies inversely here — the unnecessary fragmentation weakens code)
must_preserve: Skipper, FatalChecker, StepCallbacks semantic behavior (currently encoded on builtStep).

smell: setup.DefaultOptions has the Default* naming pattern common for 'zero-arg constructor of a defaulted options struct'. Other phase packages use NewOptions(cfg, projectRoot). The same repo mixes: postinstall.DefaultTimeout (constant, fine), install.DefaultBootstrapTimeout (constant), but setup.DefaultOptions (function). A reader can't tell whether Default* prefixed symbols are values or functions at a glance.
severity_reason: Naming consistency. Rename to setup.NewOptions(cfg, projectRoot) and the three *Options factories all share the same name.
fix_summary: Rename setup.DefaultOptions -> setup.NewOptions; accept (cfg, projectRoot) and fold ResolveReleaseBaseURL call inside. Single call site in okd.go updates. Aligns with opt-inconsistent-cfg-opts finding.
rule_source: Go naming convention: `New*` for constructors; `Default*` for values
must_preserve: DefaultOptions' current field defaults (WorkDir, DownloadDir).

smell: K8sClient is used in monitor.go only for ApprovePendingCSRs. Rather than accepting a concrete *cluster.K8sClient in MonitorInstallation, the caller could define a tiny consumer-side interface `type csrApprover interface { ApprovePendingCSRs(context.Context) (int, error) }` at the install package. This would be in line with 'accept interfaces, return structs' and make MonitorInstallation testable without a real kubectl.
severity_reason: A tiny interface at the consumer would simplify a future test helper. Not a current bug.
fix_summary: Inside install package define `type csrApprover interface { ApprovePendingCSRs(ctx context.Context) (int, error) }`. Accept it as a parameter to MonitorInstallation, defaulting to NewK8sClient(...). In tests, pass a fake.
must_preserve: Current kubectl/oc detection behavior in NewK8sClient.

smell: addon.NewManager uses four positional args (cfg, exec, logger, projectRoot). The three fields exec/logger/projectRoot all have natural 'With*' options in sibling packages (executor.WithLogger, okd.WithProjectRoot, okd.WithLogger). Adding a fifth required field (e.g. a retry budget, a namespace override) breaks every caller.
severity_reason: Purely convention. Two call sites means the migration cost is trivial; the long-term maintainability win matches okd.New/proxmox.New.
fix_summary: Convert to `func NewManager(cfg *config.Config, opts ...ManagerOption) *Manager`. Provide WithExecutor, WithLogger (defaulting to NopLogger), WithProjectRoot.
must_preserve: The InstallAll/InstallOne/Uninstall method semantics (they do not change).
